heroHeadline: Trump Brokers 3-Day Ceasefire + 1,000-for-1,000 Prisoner Exchange on Victory Day — Russia's Parade Has No Tanks for First Time in ~20 Years
heroSubtitle: On May 9, 2026 — Russia's Victory Day — the US brokered a 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11) and the largest prisoner exchange of 2026: 1,000-for-1,000, confirmed by Zelensky and Russian presidential aide Ushakov. Simultaneously, Russia's Moscow parade was stripped of all tanks, missiles, and military hardware for the first time in nearly two decades — a direct result of Ukraine's deep-strike drone campaign — while North Korean troops marched in Red Square. Putin declared 'Victory will be ours,' invoking NATO as the adversary. Despite the ceasefire, Ukraine documented 850+ Russian drone attacks overnight and 140+ front-line violations; Russia claimed 1,630 Ukrainian violations by noon. Ukraine struck a Russian oil facility in Yaroslavl 1,200 km inside Russia. Zelensky framed the prisoner exchange as Ukraine's true Victory Day: 'Red Square is less important to us than the lives of Ukrainian prisoners who can be brought home.' Day 1,535 of the full-scale invasion.
